# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | white |
| green | green |
| red | blue |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel 5 wires, positions 1 through 5, and a display and light on the board but I cannot see them. Waiting for instructions on what to do. Please tell me which wire to cut once you know.

I need to think about the communication chain here. I have the manual (light → wire color mapping), but I can't speak, so I can't tell Blind anything directly. Deaf can see the light and markings but can't hear me. My only channel is gestures to Deaf.

So the flow must be: Deaf sees the light color and reports it (speaks) - but wait, Deaf comes after me in turn order (Blind, Mute, Deaf), so Deaf will speak after seeing my gesture, and that speech would need to reach Blind next round.

I don't yet know what light is lit - only Deaf can see that. I need to wait for Deaf to tell me (via gesture) what light color they see, then I translate using the manual and gesture back the wire color, and Deaf then speaks the wire color to Blind.

Since I have no information from Deaf yet about the light color, I cannot act meaningfully yet. I should wait this turn.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | white |
| green | green |
| red | blue |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display reads 0. Light is yellow. Wires left to right: 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue.
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: Display 0, Light yellow, Wire1 green, Wire2 white, Wire3 red, Wire4 yellow, Wire5 blue. I need the manual's cutting instructions. If you cannot speak, please gesture the answer to Deaf so Deaf can relay it to me in words.

Now I know: Light is yellow → cut wire color red (per manual). Wire3 is red. So the correct wire to cut is position 3.

I need to gesture this to Deaf, who can then speak it to Blind next round. I need a way to encode "position 3" using gestures. Deaf can see gestures but not hear me, and gestures carry no inherent meaning until established. Let me use a simple counting convention: number gestures with ✌ style — I'll use finger-count gestures with a clear symbol for "position" indicator.

I'll use ☝ (one), ✌ (two), 🤟 (three)... actually let me just use a straightforward count of a single repeated symbol to indicate the number, prefaced by a distinguishing gesture to mean "cut wire number".

I'll define: 👉 means "wire position", followed by that many ☝ gestures to count it out.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👉", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

Blind says to Mute: Still waiting for the manual's instructions. Please gesture the rule to Deaf (e.g. which color/order to cut) and Deaf, please translate that gesture into words for me since I cannot see gestures.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Understood, wire 3 red confirmed. What should Blind do with it - cut it, or something else? Gesture if you can indicate an action.
Blind says to Mute: Deaf tells me wire 3 (red) seems important per your manual check. My only possible action is cut(position=N). Please confirm clearly: should I cut wire 3? Gesture a thumbs up to Deaf for yes, thumbs down for no, and have Deaf relay it to me in words.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```


Blind says to Mute: Cutting wire 3 as confirmed.

The bomb changed - I need new information from Deaf about the current state (new light color, wires, display) before I can give further instructions.


Deaf says: Success! Wire 3 was cut correctly, bomb changed. New state: Display 0, light now green. Wires: 1 white, 2 yellow, 3 CUT, 4 blue, 5 green.
Blind says to Mute: Wire 3 cut successfully. New state: display 0, light green, wires: 1 white, 2 yellow, 3 CUT, 4 blue, 5 green. Is the bomb defused, or does the manual require another action? Please advise.

New light is green → cut wire color green (per manual). Wire5 is green. So target is position 5.

I'll use the same established gesture convention: 👉 followed by counting ☝ five times, then 👍 to confirm/approve action.


Blind says to Mute: Wire 1 cut successfully. New state: display 0, light red, wires: 1 CUT, 2 white, 3 CUT, 4 blue, 5 CUT. Only 2 and 4 remain. Please advise next step.
